discovery: Observational discovery of the galaxy population in the early universe and the charting of cosmic history back to the epoch of reionization

nominees.name: Garth D. Illingworth
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Santa Cruz, USA

motivation: Until the 1990s, galaxies in the young universe were almost entirely unseen. Charles Steidel's Lyman-break technique showed that large numbers of star-forming galaxies existed within the first few billion years after the Big Bang, and it made them a population that could be studied systematically. Garth Illingworth took the lead in extending the search through Hubble's deepest infrared imaging, identifying galaxies within about 500 million years of the Big Bang and measuring how their abundance changed with time. Richard Ellis pioneered spectroscopic and gravitational-lensing studies that confirmed distances and tied these first galaxies to the reionization of intergalactic hydrogen. Together they turned cosmic dawn from speculation into an observational science. They set the strategy that JWST now carries into the first few hundred million years, and they established how the universe's first luminous structures formed.
